subject: general
question: _________ was the first governor-general of Bengal.
solution:
Correct Answer Warren Hasting

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 till he resigned in the year 1785.
 
• He was a writer or can be called a clerk in the early stages of his career in the East India Company at Calcutta in 1750.
 
• He became the British resident at Murshidabad, the capital of Bengal in the year 1758 after Mir Jafar was appointed as the Nawab after the Battle of Plassey.
 
• During his tenure, the first Anglo-Maratha and the second Anglo-Mysore and wars were fought.
 
• In the year 1773, the Regulating Act of 1773 was passed during his period.
 
• He gave support to Sir William Jones in the formation of the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1785.
 
• 
 
Warren Hastings abolished the dual system of government which was started by Robert Clive.

 

Hence, the first Governor General of Bengal was Warren Hasting__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**William Bentinck (1828-35):

__
 
• ​Appointed as the Governor of Madras in 1803.
 
• He was recalled to Britain after the Vellore mutiny in 1806.
 
 
• Cause of Vellore mutiny: Ban on putting caste symbols on forehead & wear of earrings by soldiers.
 
 
 
• On 04/12/1829, he issued a Regulation XVII prohibiting the practice of Sati or widow burning.
 
• Suppression of thugs was undertaken by Colonel Sleeman from 1830 under his reign.
 
• He took effective measures against female infanticide & made it a punishable offence.
 
 
• He prohibited child sacrifice at Saugar island in Bengal.
 
 
 
• He abolished the provincial court of appeal established by Cornwallis.
 
• He introduced local languages in lower courts & English in higher courts instead of Persian.
 
• He introduced the Mahalwari Land Revenue System in UP, Central Province, Punjab.

Charles Metcalfe

 
• ​Sir Charles Metcalfe (1835-1836) is known as the press liberator.
 
• The Governor-General of India has been dubbed the "Liberator of the Indian Press” because he lifted restrictions on press freedom.

John Shore (1793-1798) -__

 
• John Shore, also known as Lord Teignmouth, was the third Governor-General of India, serving from 1793 to 1798.
 
• He continued the administrative and judicial reforms initiated by his predecessors and played an important role in the establishment of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
